linkedin_activity.text: 80% adoption is not a technology story. It is a human experience story. Fortune just featured Emmanuel Frenehard on how Sanofi is building its own AI ecosystem on our data, our terms, our standard for what good looks like. Those of us on his leadership team are not surprised. What I want to add is the Consumer Experience (CX) lens. When 80% of Sanofi's global workforce uses #Concierge , every interaction is a signal. Did it feel intuitive? Did it earn trust? Did it reflect who Sanofi is? That is the CX question behind every AI decision we make. Human-centered AI means our experiences should feel distinctly ours. Not a pharma template. Not a vendor default. Designed around the humans we serve, created for our employees, our patients, our caregivers, our Health Care Providers. At Sanofi , we build human experiences, powered by AI. That is the work. Hat trick. Three iF Design Awards. Two products changing lives. We are beyond proud to announce that Sanofi has won three prestigious iF Design Awards in the Healthcare category, recognized for our ecosystem approach to patient, HCP and caregiver experience and care, and our UX/UI research, strategy and design across Tzield and Dupixent. But let's be clear about what this recognition is really about. It's about a child whose Type 1 diabetes is detected earlier because we designed an experience that makes that possible. It's about a patient who doesn't abandon a treatment they need because we removed the friction, the confusion, and the fear standing in their way. It's about what happens when you start with the human, not the product, not the technology, not the process, and build everything else around them. That is the Sanofi approach. Consumer first. Always. These awards validate something our teams have believed from day one: that great design in healthcare is not a luxury or an aesthetic choice. It is a clinical and human imperative. When the experience is broken, patients disengage. When the experience works, outcomes improve. Tzield and Dupixent are two of many patient-first experiences we continue to design and build. This is not a finish line. It is a signal of the standard we hold ourselves to, and a commitment to every patient whose life we have the opportunity to make better. Huge congratulations to the incredible teams behind this work. You didn't just win awards. You built something that matters. 3 days. 1 event. Many lessons, and a few robots 😜. I just wrapped up VivaTech 2026 and I’m still processing the energy of this place. I had the privilege of being on stage for the Financial Times Sovereign AI panel, also sharing the Sanofi AI strategy at the Sanofi booth, and diving into how #AI and #quantumcomputing are reshaping the future at the Black Stage, from drug discovery to the very fabric of how industries will operate. But beyond the panels, what struck me most were the conversations in between. A few thoughts I’m bringing home: 🧠 #AI has helped humans become “smarter” and more efficient. The next frontier: can it help us become wiser? Intelligence without wisdom is just optimization. The question we should be asking is not only what AI can do, but what it should do, and for whom. 🔓 #Data sharing needs to be de-demonized. Yes, there are real principles and non-negotiables around data protection. But fear shouldn’t be the default. Trusted, purposeful data sharing is one of the most powerful levers we have. Let’s govern it well — not avoid it. 🏛️ The launch of the European Centre of AI Excellence in Paris is a signal. #Europe is not just watching the AI race. It’s finally choosing to shape it with sovereignty, responsibility, and ambition. Very proud to have been invited to the discussion. 🌍 And one unexpected highlight: a rich exchange with the Turkish delegation. A clear appetite to position #Turkey as a serious #AI player on the global stage. These are the conversations that remind you how global this #transformation truly is. 🤖 And yes, I had a lot of fun with my robot peers. (They didn’t steal my panel slot. This time.) But honestly? The moment that hit me hardest wasn’t on stage. A company is not a name. It’s a purpose. And it’s the people carrying it. I want to take a moment to acknowledge Emmanuel Frenehard a leader with a bold vision, who genuinely believes in the power of Data & AI to transform Sanofi, and who gave me the space, the trust, and the stage to make it happen. That kind of sponsorship is rare. I don’t take it for granted. And to my peers, specially the maestro of Ai adoption and fun Florent Edouard at the booth and my team: you know who you are. This is ours. 🙏 Grateful, energized, and ready for what’s next. 🚀 Julien Marcaut you are the maestro behind the scene for organizing all this. thank you 🙏 #VivaTech #AI #DataStrategy #SovereignAI #Sanofi #QuantumComputing #EuropeanAI #Leadership #DataSharing #Grateful

Today marks my final day at Sanofi Japan. It has been six and a half years since I joined in September 2019. During this time, we have continuously faced unprecedented and unpredictable challenges and changes. These experiences have become invaluable lessons for me. I have always kept the question "Am I truly contributing to patients?" at the center of my work, engaging in dialogue with my Sanofi colleagues and tackling challenges together. I feel that I have come this far because of the irreplaceable presence of these wonderful teammates. At Sanofi, we are united as an organization with the mission to "pursue the miracles of science and improve people's lives." To deliver innovative medicines and vaccines to as many patients as possible, and to address social challenges, our employees are taking the lead in pioneering initiatives. I am confident that this excellent culture will continue to develop and flourish. I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to all the employees who have walked this journey with me over the past six and a half years, as well as to healthcare professionals, government officials, industry partners, and everyone else who has supported me along the way. Thank you so much. Regardless of where our paths take us, I look forward to continuing our shared commitment to improving patients' lives. This week, the North Europe Specialty Care Leadership Team came together to align on our Priorities, and we ended it with what I can honestly say was the "best team building I have ever done." We visited the OnlyFriends Sportsclub in Amsterdam - and from the moment we arrived, the story of this place moved us deeply. It all started in 2000 with one father's love, when Dennis Gebbink watched his son being sidelined at football because of his motor disability. So he built something better. Today, the OnlyFriends Sportsclub is a like giant family – more than 950 children and 100 elderly members sporting together across around 35 sports, 7 days a week, powered by 200+ volunteers who give their time out of pure dedication. This year they celebrate 26 years and they have an even bigger ambition? Be a 100 more years old! Their motto is just as powerful: "Je bent goed zoals je bent!" - You are good just the way you are. One of the volunteers, already there for 15 years and who started thanks to his father, made us tour the incredible OnlyFriends Sports facilities – one of the only sports facilities fully dedicated to children with disabilities in Europe, with even a sports and lifestyle prosthetics making facility. And then we took to the court ourselves for a wheelchair basketball session. We were coached by one of their dedicated volunteers - living with ALS himself. His story alone was a masterclass in resilience, courage, and the power of giving back. The competitive spirit in our team emerged instantly, but it was humility, inspiration and admiration that stayed with us long after we left the court. This is why OnlyFriends resonates so deeply with our mission at Sanofi. We chase the miracles of science to help people live their fullest lives. OnlyFriends proves every single day that when you create a space where everyone truly belongs - magic happens. It is more than team building. It is purpose building. 💙 👉 www.onlyfriends.nl Sportclub Only Friends #friendshipsportscenter #onlyfriends Michaela Nygårdas, PhD Maartje Jacobs Pauline Malfait Aleksander Ingero Hanne Mette Tell Elaine Ji Lorraine Hamilton Sebahate Shala

Earlier this week, I was honored to receive the PM360 Magazine Uber ELITE Award, which recognizes innovation, leadership, and a commitment to advancing healthcare in the US. Looking at the names of past winners — many of whom are giants who shaped this industry — I feel the weight of this honor. I’m especially grateful to Anna S. and Jon Brulloths for organizing the event, and thankful to George Dickens , Dan Dovdavany and Jane Brunn for attending. Over the past four years in the US, I’ve had the privilege of working alongside an extraordinary team, guided by a few core leadership principles: - Transparency builds trust—and trust accelerates everything. When trust is present, teams move faster, collaborate more effectively, and take smarter risks. - Balance ambition with relentless execution. Vision without follow-through is only a wish. - Bring energy and joy to the work (my friend Shawn Achor will definitely agree with that statement!). We operate in demanding environments, but when people feel proud of what they do, that’s when innovation thrives and performance becomes extraordinary. Together we shape the future, asking ourselves one essential question: how can I improve patients' lives? That people-first mindset, that is how we decide and act...and that's what this recognition is really about.
